tasks.title: Plain JSON validation regains baseline CPU performance and rejects inherited array elements
tasks.spec: ## Repository: contract, Behavior in full (required behavior 1-5, test-first steps 1-3 and the CPU script), Files, Checks and Completion evidence; ## Counterexamples 1-14 and CPU statistic; ## Security impact, ## Non-goals and ## Rollout order. Implement the compiled schema walk using captured built-ins and technique A (descriptors) or B (lookupGetter/lookupSetter behind the per-call call integrity check), always copying object values at record schemas, top-level ownValue read, Proxy test/comment change, docs, version 1.7.1 and regenerated build output together. The bench test changes only if its fixture shapes move into the CPU script; README changes only if it repeats the own-data or Proxy rule on the implementation branch. Include any other dist file regenerated by the build. If the branch already rejects cases 1-2 and parses certified plain JSON without copying, request the hold specified in Behavior rather than proceeding to review.

acceptance.expected: Bun reports 1.4.0; installation exits 0 with the existing lockfile. zod stays pinned to 4.6.7 as the only runtime dependency; no tooling, dependency, schema, type, public export or WIRE_VERSION change.

Test-first evidence on unchanged source at 7ce23aaf3fa3e038f65ecfed755188b83bde143f, after adding counterexamples: cases 1 and 2 are red because top-level inherited elements are accepted. Case 1 includes uptime and latency. Cases 3, 4, 9, 11, 13 and 14 and guards 5-8, 10 and 12 pass. Each case uses exported validators and the literal errors, verdicts, identities and counts in Counterexamples. Record the failing test names and assertions in the PR.

Historical-walk red evidence: temporarily apply exactly the Counterexamples recipe to 7ce23aa, copying ebcbbb6 src/validate.ts lines 189-312 except the duplicate lookupGetter at 195-197, enabling isOwnData in problem and leaving arrayProblem unchanged. Run the full suite, including admin and tokens. New cases 1-4, 9, 13 and 14 fail; each of 13a-c returns ok:true with getter count 1 instead of 0; 13d returns check.headers: must be an object; 14a-c count above 0 (Verified state reports 363, 16 and 363 respectively). Existing red tests are the eight admin tests named in Verified state (original lines 397, 465, 510, 559, 637, 662, 689, 710), tokens 'array elements count only as own data properties' (283), the old descriptor/get Proxy test (313, if not yet replaced), and smoke 'dist matches a fresh build of src' for the unbuilt source. The replacement Proxy test may pass. Guards 5-8, 10 and 12 pass. Record the actual failing names, compare with Behavior step 2 and report any additional existing failure. Revert the temporary walk before implementing; never commit it.

acceptance.command: bun test test/validate.test.ts test/http-options.test.ts test/tokens.test.ts test/audit.test.ts test/admin.test.ts
acceptance.expected: On the candidate, 0 fail in selected tests; a focused run may fail the global coverage threshold, whose gate is the full suite. Counterexamples 1-14 pass, with case 11 supplied by unchanged existing tests. Cases 1-2 reject inherited top-level elements with uptime[1]: must be an object, latency[1]: must be an object and uptime[0]: must be an object. Cases 3-4 reject nested inherited days at uptime[0].days[89], latency[0].days[89], uptime.days[89] and uptime[1].days[89] with is required. Holes, accessor elements/fields, inherited checkId, setter-only checkId and repeat validation after accessor/hole mutation have the exact Counterexamples 5-8 and 10 errors; all getter counts are 0. Enumerable Object.prototype.extra preserves validateComponent ok:true. Dense JSON, null-prototype items and non-enumerable own declared fields return ok:true with value identical to input. Existing own-data tests for unions, recursive JSON, record keys and non-plain prototypes remain green.

0 fail in selected tests; focused coverage is not the full-suite gate. Counterexample 13a-d each uses the JSON HTTP check with headers X-Key:v and Auth:{env:PULSE_HEADER_A}. Non-enumerable Object.prototype constructor getter, arrow constructor plus prototype getter, hasOwnProperty getter, and deletion of Object.prototype.isPrototypeOf each yield ok:true, value === c and count === 0. Counterexample 14b replaces Function.prototype.call with a counting getter and validates the specified JSON HTTP check without headers: ok:true, input identity and count === 0. Restore every saved prototype descriptor in finally, deleting only properties newly added by the test. These tests exercise the exported validateCheck.

0 fail in selected tests; focused coverage is not the full-suite gate. Counterexample 14a replaces Function.prototype.call with a counting getter; 14c adds an own call getter to Object.prototype.__lookupGetter__. Each calls validateCheckUptime(item) directly on a valid 90-day item, expects ok:true, value === item and count === 0, and restores descriptors in finally. Do not use validateUptimeResponse for these probes: the existing top-level arrayProblem call lookup is a known limit.

Review against Required behavior 1-5: schema-cached compiled walks, no trust cached by input, indexed loops over precompiled keys and no input copies. The walk calls only module-load captured built-ins; no run-time global Object.x/Array.x call or unchecked call/apply lookup. Technique A permits only transient descriptors per value and uses captured hasOwn(descriptor,'value'), never 'value' in descriptor. Technique B allocates nothing per value and checks both getters and setters only after a once-per-problem-call descriptor/prototype integrity check: Function.prototype.call is the captured own data function, and both captured lookup functions have the captured Function.prototype and no own call. Unsafe integrity falls back to the copy. Every non-array object at a record schema always fails certification; the walk calls neither Object.keys nor Reflect.ownKeys. Preserve wrapper, prototype, own-data, setter, absent-key/inherited-key, union and lazy rules; check enumerable Object.prototype string keys once per problem call. Certification preserves copy-path verdict/error text and adds no getter or function execution. arrayProblem uses ownValue(value,i), preserving its accessor error and existing lookupGetter.call check. The sole removed assertions belong to the named descriptor/get Proxy test, replaced with no-throw and typeof result.ok === boolean checks for every original validator call; hostile-trap and cyclic-prototype tests stay unchanged.

acceptance.command: for round in 1 2 3; do bun "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT/test/validate-cpu.ts" "$CONTRACT_A_ROOT" || exit; bun "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT/test/validate-cpu.ts" "$CONTRACT_B_ROOT" || exit; done
acceptance.expected: All 6 fresh processes exit 0, ordered A,B,A,B,A,B, using the identical candidate script against each root/src/index.ts. The script narrows imported validators from unknown without any; each fixture is JSON-parsed before timing and has 1000 checks x 90 days from 2026-01-01 with the literal uptime/latency values in CPU statistic. Assert ok:true and value === input before timing, then 2 warmups and 7 process.cpuUsage user+system samples per workload. Each process prints one JSON line {root,bun,uptime:{samples,median},latency:{samples,median}}; median is the 4th-smallest sample. Per workload, side values are the 2nd-smallest of 3 invocation medians. Using unrounded values, B <= 1.10 * A for both workloads. Report all 3x7 raw samples per side/workload, invocation medians, side values rounded to 0.01 ms and (B/A-1)*100 rounded to 0.1%; keep the 10% bound and all safety checks.

acceptance.expected: All 6 fresh processes exit 0 using the same CPU method. Report the additional A/B of today's main 7ce23aa against the candidate, with samples, medians and percentage changes; this comparison is evidence of the gain and is not the gating baseline.

PR body contains Completion evidence: test-first failures on 7ce23aa for 1-2; full-suite historical-walk failures for 3,4,9,11,13,14 compared with the specified list (including 13a-c count 1, 13d type error and 14a-c counts above 0); guards 5-8,10,12 passing on 7ce23aa; final green test names/commands and bun run check output; name of the sole replaced Proxy test; both CPU A/Bs with exact commands, full SHAs, machine/Bun details, raw samples and derived statistics. Name technique A or B and the module-level constants captured by the walk. Record findings for all applicable Security impact items (input validation, accessor/function execution, unchanged errors without secrets) and hostile inputs: polluted Object/Array prototypes, record constructor/prototype/hasOwnProperty variants, deleted Object.prototype.isPrototypeOf and own constructor keys, getters on Function.prototype.call, Function.prototype.apply, Object.hasOwn and Object.getPrototypeOf at history validators, frozen/subclass arrays, null-prototype objects and hostile Proxies. For every polluted global compare verdict, text and getter counts to 7ce23aa: same verdict/text and no added getter calls. State known limits: disagreeing Proxy traps are out of scope but never throw, existing propertyIsEnumerable pollution and top-level arrayProblem lookupGetter.call behavior are not fixed, records always take the copy path and gains reach consumers only on their later pin updates. No compose or service startup check applies to this library-only change.
